Stated Claim / Post Context:
Warming trend with windy days takes over this week

Temperatures will climb steadily through the week, reaching the low to mid 60s by Tuesday and Wednesday before a storm system brings rain chances back to the region Friday into the weekend.

Actual Article Body:
LINCOLN, Neb. (KOLN) - After a quiet and cool Sunday, a warming trend is about to take over the forecast area. Temperatures will climb steadily through the week, reaching the low to mid 60s by Tuesday and Wednesday before a storm system brings rain chances back to the region Friday into the weekend.

Right now, high pressure is keeping things peaceful across the area. We’ll have one more morning where low temperatures fall to about the freezing mark before you can expect another relatively calm day Monday with a mix of clouds and sunshine.

Temperatures will gradually warm from the upper 50s on Monday to about 60° Tuesday, then hit the low to mid 60s by Wednesday.

It’s the kind of weather that makes you want to get outside in November.

However, there’s a catch: winds will pick up, especially Tuesday and Wednesday. Gusts could reach 35 to 45+ mph, with the strongest winds expected in northeast Nebraska.

A cold front will push through Wednesday evening, bringing a small chance of rain to the area. Right now, we’re only looking at a 20-30% chance of showers, mainly near and east of the Missouri River. Don’t expect much — any rain that falls will be light and spotty.

The real story is the storm system heading our way for the end of the week. A strong trough will dig into the western U.S. by Thursday and move through our area on Saturday. This system will bring more widespread rain chances Friday night into Saturday as it moves through.

Long-range models bring much of the rain through central and eastern Nebraska in that window, but timing and track of this system are still details we are digging into. Below, you’re looking at decent agreement between a couple long-range models as of Sunday afternoon for the track of the system.

But we’ll be watching for any changes and alterations to the forecast with time as we get closer because it would have implications on Nebraska’s last home game of the season against Ohio State.

Because again, there’s still some uncertainty about the exact track and timing of this system, but the overall trend suggests we’ll see showers and possibly a few storms as the system passes. The good news? Any snow associated with this system should stay well to our northwest, so we’re looking at rain here, not snow.
